This vignette is the short path to **`cams()`**: estimands, assumptions,
Bayesian and REML inference on the same model, and the main summaries.
Contribution-adjusted meta-analysis (CAMS) is the treatment-by-subgroup
interaction model developed in @panaro2025cams. For additional shipped
datasets (`age`, `edss`, `il6`, RESPIRE), see
[`vignette("worked-examples")`](worked-examples.html). For tables you can
QC or hand to reporting, see
[`vignette("export-and-qc")`](export-and-qc.html).

## Estimands (what CAMS reports)

| Estimand | Function | Depends on reporting IF? |
|----------|----------|--------------------------|
| Treatment-by-subgroup **interaction** $\gamma$ | **`interactions()`** | No |
| **Modifier-level** mean effects $\mu_A(\pi)$, $\mu_B(\pi)$ | **`modifiers()`** | Yes (default pooled $\widetilde{\pi}$) |
| **Combined-population** mean $M(\pi)$ | **`combined()`** | Yes |
| Trial **information fractions** $\pi_j$ | **`ifrac()`** (optional before fit) | Built inside **`cams()`** by default |

The **reference** modifier (e.g. NIV vs IV) sets the direction of
$\gamma$. All fits are on the **escalc** scale (`yi`, `vi`); use
**`exponentiate = TRUE`** for odds ratios, hazard ratios, or other
ratio measures.

## Scope and key assumptions

**Intended use.** CAMS synthesises **aggregate subgroup effects across
trials** (published tables, systematic reviews, HTA-style evidence
pools). It is **not** a substitute for a pre-specified subgroup analysis
in a single randomised trial SAP.

**Data.** Long format: one row per trial × modifier with **`yi`** and
**`vi`**. Use **`escalc()`** (re-exported from **metafor** [@viechtbauer2010])
when starting from event counts.

**Within-trial sampling.** The implementation treats the two modifier
estimates in a trial as **conditionally independent** with variances
**`vi`**, and uses precision-based **information fractions** $\pi_j$.
Shared control arms, nested subgroups, or other **within-trial
dependence** are **not** modelled yet (see **`?cams`**, section on sampling
assumption).

**Between-trial heterogeneity.** Separate random-effects components for
the interaction contrasts and the combined-effect meta-regression
[@panaro2025cams]; see **`heterogeneity()`** after fit.

## Example: COVID steroids (IV / NIV)

The **`steroids`** data are mortality **odds ratios** by ventilation
subgroup (IV vs NIV) from the REACT meta-analysis [@stern2020react]. Rows with **`n = 0`**
mark unreported subgroups; **`ifrac()`** completes the table for CAMS
(see [`vignette("worked-examples")`](worked-examples.html), **`il6`**
section).

```{r data, warning=FALSE, message=FALSE}
library(interactmeta)
library(dplyr)

steroids_obs <- steroids |> filter(n > 0)
steroids_es <- escalc(
  measure = "OR",
  ai = treat.events,
  bi = treat.total - treat.events,
  ci = cont.events,
  di = cont.total - cont.events,
  data = steroids_obs
)
des <- ifrac(steroids_es, reference = "NIV")
```

## One model, two inference backends

**`cams()`** specifies the same CAMS likelihood; choose **Bayesian**
(default, **bayesmeta** [@rover2020]) or **frequentist**
(**`method = "REML"`**, **metafor** [@viechtbauer2010]). Below we fit
both on **`des`** with **`reference = "NIV"`**. The half-normal scales on
$\tau_m$ and $\tau_g$ follow @panaro2026priors (not the package defaults,
which are improper uniform priors on heterogeneity).

```{r fit-both, cache = TRUE}
fit_bayes <- cams(
  des,
  reference = "NIV",
  tau.prior = function(tau) bayesmeta::dhalfnormal(tau, scale = 0.5),
  tau.interaction.prior = function(tau) bayesmeta::dhalfnormal(tau, scale = 0.1)
)
fit_reml <- cams(des, reference = "NIV", method = "REML")
```

The interaction **does not** depend on the reporting information
fraction. Modifier and combined summaries **do**; they use the pooled
reporting $\widetilde{\pi}$ from **`ifrac(fit)`** by default.

```{r mirror-interaction}
ix_b <- tidy(interactions(fit_bayes, type = "Overall", exponentiate = TRUE))
ix_r <- tidy(interactions(fit_reml, type = "Overall", exponentiate = TRUE))
knitr::kable(
  bind_rows(Bayesian = ix_b, REML = ix_r, .id = "inference") |>
    select(inference, type, estimate, conf.low, conf.high),
  digits = 2,
  caption = "Interaction (OR scale): Bayesian credible vs REML confidence intervals"
)
```

Bayesian and REML CAMS intervals are comparable. Bayesian credible
intervals use the DIRECT quadrature mixture [@rover2017direct]; they
reflect heterogeneity uncertainty and the priors above. REML intervals
are Wald confidence intervals from the stored **`metafor`** fit
[@viechtbauer2010].

```{r estimands-reml}
interactions(fit_reml, type = "Overall", exponentiate = TRUE)
modifiers(fit_reml, type = "Overall", exponentiate = TRUE)
combined(fit_reml, type = "Overall", exponentiate = TRUE)
ifrac(fit_reml, ifrac = "interaction")
```

## Forest plot (reporting checklist)

**`forestplot()`** draws observed modifier estimates, optional shrinkage,
and **Overall** / **Prediction** summaries at $\widetilde{\pi}$. For
publication-style figures, set **`exponentiate = TRUE`**, **`favours`**
text, and keep table numbers from **`tidy(modifiers(...))`** aligned
with the pooled diamonds.

```{r forest, fig.width = 8, fig.height = 5, cache = TRUE}
forestplot(
  fit_reml,
  exponentiate = TRUE,
  favours = c("Lower mortality", "Higher mortality")
)
```

**Caption ingredients:** population (critically ill COVID-19), estimand
(OR for mortality by ventilation subgroup), **CAMS** with **`method =
"REML"`**, reference **NIV**, reporting IF from **`ifrac(fit_reml)`**,
interval type (Wald CI for REML).
